scenes.text: In nineteen sixty-seven, a student found a signal from space so regular that it was nicknamed little green men.
Her name was Jocelyn Bell, a twenty-four-year-old graduate student at Cambridge.
She and other students had built a huge radio telescope covering about four and a half acres.
Checking the chart paper by hand, she spotted a tiny wiggle she called a bit of scruff.
On November twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven, a faster recording showed what it really was.
A sharp pulse, repeating about every one point three seconds, like a cosmic clock.
Nothing natural was known to tick that precisely, so the team jokingly labeled it L G M one.
Then she found a second ticking signal, in a completely different part of the sky.
Two sets of aliens seemed unlikely, so the alien idea faded.
The real source was a pulsar, a spinning neutron star only about ten miles across.
Its beams sweep past Earth like a lighthouse.
Her supervisor Antony Hewish shared the nineteen seventy-four Nobel Prize in Physics, but she was left out.
Would you have guessed aliens too? Tell me below.

title: A student found 'little green men' in space 👽
caption: On Nov 28, 1967, Cambridge student Jocelyn Bell confirmed a radio signal pulsing every 1.3 seconds. Her team jokingly called it LGM-1, but it turned out to be the first pulsar ever found.
